elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Retained sentence: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party." AP (Customer) therefore has a no-cause exit, albeit only after the 1-year Initial Term. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false, but that is a literal-string artefact (the clause uses "Either Party" rather than "Customer may terminate"); in substance the Customer convenience right exists.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is "ninety (90) days written notice"; no 30-day Customer notice was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic exists; the retained sentence runs the other way: "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement". A pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is neither present nor added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso: "provided that any termination by Kubient shall be effective only at the end of the then-current Term." The effective date is expressly anchored to term-end, so Kubient cannot exit mid-Term for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band and applies to AP unchanged by the edit.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere in paragraph 4; the only termination-linked payment is "all fees generated during the termination period", i.e. ordinary revenue-share fees earned through the 90-day notice window, which cannot exceed three months' fees. The conditional element is satisfied because no ETF mechanic exists to cap. (Note for the drafter: "termination period" is not a defined term; if Kubient ever argued it extended beyond the 90-day notice window this element would become uncertain, so a clarifying "i.e., the ninety (90) day notice period" could be raised in negotiation, though it is not required to complete the checklist.)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The added proviso ties Kubient's termination effectiveness expressly to term-end: "any termination by Kubient shall be effective only at the end of the then-current Term." This is the anchoring the playbook requires; the pre-edit mutual notice right alone would not have sufficed.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The mutual notice requirement "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" binds Kubient as well as AP and is left verbatim.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Customer keeps a 90-day no-cause exit after the Initial Term, no early-termination fee exists (only fees earned through the notice window), Kubient must give 90 days' notice, and the inserted proviso now anchors any Kubient convenience termination to the end of the then-current Term — the single material term on which the original clause failed the fallback.

Preferred level is not reached: notice remains 90 days (not 30) and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. That is a defensible election given the revenue-share structure with no prepaid fees, and the drafter says so; it simply means the redline lands at fallback, which the playbook accepts.

Minimality holds: a single proviso is appended to the existing sentence; the Initial Term lock, the mutual 90-day notice, the fee-entitlement sentence and the 4(b) breach/insolvency rights are retained verbatim, with no survival tails, refund mechanics, 'in whole or in part' surplus or other extras added.
Intent is preserved: the auto-renewal, revenue-share fee entitlement and cure-period mechanics survive without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting tightening (not a checklist defect): the proviso reads "any termination by Kubient", which grammatically attaches to the for-any-reason sentence but could be argued to reach Kubient's 4(b) breach and immediate insolvency terminations. Consider "provided that any termination by Kubient under this sentence shall be effective only at the end of the then-current Term" to foreclose that reading; the ambiguity currently cuts in our favour, so it is not a barrier to sending.
